idiom_name: sealed service class with constructor-injected collaborators (registered with built-in DI)
implementation_notes: C# offers no shortcut: write a sealed class (or an interface plus implementation when alternate subsystems must be substitutable) whose methods coordinate the collaborators passed to its constructor, and resolve it through Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection instead of a static accessor. The BCL shows the shape with static facades - System.IO.File delegates file operations to FileStream and the OS - but such static classes are not injectable, so when the subsystem itself is static, wrap it behind your own interface before anyone depends on it. The class structure stays hand-written; DI wiring is what keeps it testable.
pitfalls: Static facades such as System.IO.File cannot be substituted, so tests hit the real file system; inject an interface-backed wrapper instead.
Registering a singleton facade that captures scoped or transient collaborators causes lifetime and thread-safety bugs in DI containers - align the lifetimes.
Swallowing exceptions inside the facade breaks the caller's ability to compensate (rollback, retry, user feedback).
A facade that returns EF entities or open streams leaks subsystem lifecycle to callers; return facade-owned types and own the cleanup.
